sentences.en: Last week on the show, we featured the story of Randy Gardner,
sentences.zh: 在上周的节目中，我们讲述了兰迪·加德纳的故事，

sentences.en: a San Diego man who went 11 days without sleeping, breaking a world record.
sentences.zh: 他是一位来自圣地亚哥的男子，在不睡觉的情况下坚持了11天，打破了世界纪录。

sentences.en: That was the thinking back in the 60s, and that's the thinking that I had.
sentences.zh: 那是60年代的想法，也是我曾经的想法。

sentences.en: Of course, as it turns out, that was absolutely wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，事实证明，那是完全错误的。

sentences.en: Randy's exploit would come back to haunt him later on in life in the form of crippling insomnia.
sentences.zh: 兰迪的壮举在后来的人生中以严重的失眠症形式困扰着他。

sentences.en: This week on the show, we continue to look at sleep and explore one of the greatest mysteries in human behavior.
sentences.zh: 在本周的节目中，我们将继续关注睡眠，并探索人类行为中最伟大的谜团之一。

sentences.en: Nature has endowed us with an amazing brain.
sentences.zh: 大自然赋予了我们一个神奇的大脑。

sentences.en: So why in the world would nature have that very same brain put itself to sleep for one-third of our lives?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么大自然会让同一个大脑在我们生命的三分之一时间里处于睡眠状态呢？

sentences.en: If we didn't need eight hours of sleep and we could survive on six,
sentences.zh: 如果我们不需要八小时的睡眠，而六小时就能生存，

sentences.en: Mother Nature would have done away with 25% of our sleep time millions of years ago.
sentences.zh: 大自然母亲在数百万年前就会取消我们25%的睡眠时间了。

sentences.en: Because when you think about it, sleep is an idiotic thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因为当你仔细想想，睡觉是一件愚蠢的事情。

sentences.en: If sleep does not provide a remarkable set of benefits,
sentences.zh: 如果睡眠不能提供一系列显著的好处，

sentences.en: then it's the biggest mistake the evolutionary process has ever made.
sentences.zh: 那么它就是进化过程中犯下的最大错误。

sentences.en: Matthew Walker is a professor of neuroscience and psychology at the University of California at Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 马修·沃克是加州大学伯克利分校的神经科学和心理学教授。

sentences.en: He studies sleep, and he's the author of the book, Why We Sleep.
sentences.zh: 他研究睡眠，也是《我们为什么要睡觉》一书的作者。

sentences.en: I started our conversation by asking him to tell me a story he describes in his book.
sentences.zh: 我开始我们的谈话时，请他讲述他在书中描述的一个故事。

sentences.en: It's about a pianist who relied on sleep for his creative process.
sentences.zh: 那是关于一位依靠睡眠来完成创作过程的钢琴家的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was giving a public lecture on sleep,
sentences.zh: 是的，当时我正在做一个关于睡眠的公开讲座，

sentences.en: and at the time we didn't know too much about sleep's role in learning and memory,
sentences.zh: 那时我们对睡眠在学习和记忆中的作用了解不多，

sentences.en: of which we now know a great deal.
sentences.zh: 而现在我们已经了解了很多。

sentences.en: And this wonderful sort of distinguished-looking gentleman with a fantastic kindly face walked to me.
sentences.zh: 然后，一位看起来很了不起、面容慈祥的绅士向我走来。

sentences.en: He's dressed in this great sort of tweed suit.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一套很棒的粗花呢西装。

sentences.en: I'm a pianist, and I was fascinated by what you were saying about sleep and how active a brain state it is.
sentences.zh: 我是一名钢琴家，你关于睡眠以及它是一种多么活跃的大脑状态的论述让我着迷。

sentences.en: And I wanted to tell you that there are times when I will be trying to learn a new piece,
sentences.zh: 我想告诉你，有时当我试图学习一首新曲子时，

sentences.en: and I just can't get it.
I make the same mistake at the same place each and every time.
sentences.zh: 我在同一个地方总是犯同样的错误。

sentences.en: And I'll sometimes play late into the evening,
and I will walk away, continuing to be frustrated,
sentences.zh: 然后我走开，依然感到沮丧，

sentences.en: And then when I come back and I sit down the next morning,
sentences.zh: 第二天早上当我回来坐下时，
我竟然能完美地演奏出来。

sentences.en: And what he was suggesting, perhaps, was that it wasn't practice that made perfect.
sentences.zh: 他所暗示的或许是，熟能生巧的并不是练习本身。

sentences.en: It was practice with a night of sleep that made perfect.
sentences.zh: 而是练习加上一夜的睡眠才成就了完美。

sentences.en: I want to run two other examples by you,
sentences.zh: 我想再向你举两个例子，

sentences.en: both of which seem to suggest that remarkable things happen to us while we're sleeping.
sentences.zh: 这两个例子似乎都表明，在我们睡觉时，神奇的事情发生了。

sentences.en: I understand the guitarist Keith Richards from Rolling Stones kept his instrument and a recorder by his bed,
sentences.zh: 我听说滚石乐队的吉他手基思·理查兹在床边放着他的乐器和录音机，

sentences.en: and he did it in case inspiration struck while he was asleep.
sentences.zh: 他这样做是为了以防在睡梦中产生灵感。

sentences.en: It did, and it's, I think, one of the wonderful stories of sleep-inspired creativity, of which there are many.
sentences.zh: 确实发生过，我认为这是睡眠激发的创造力中精彩的故事之一，这样的故事有很多。

sentences.en: He would have this tape recorder, and he would have his guitar,
sentences.zh: 他会准备好录音机，还有他的吉他，

sentences.en: and who knows what else around in the bedroom at the time.
sentences.zh: 谁知道当时卧室里还有什么其他东西。

sentences.en: And one morning, he woke up, and the tape had recorded all the way to the end,
sentences.zh: 一天早上，他醒来时，磁带已经录到了尽头，

sentences.en: and he didn't remember anything about that night.
sentences.zh: 而他对那天晚上的事情毫无记忆。

sentences.en: So he rewound the tape, and he played it, and he says, and this is in his autobiography,
sentences.zh: 于是他倒带播放，他说——这在他的自传里有记载——

sentences.en: there was almost this sort of ghostly vision of him strumming the chords to satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 磁带里几乎有一种幽灵般的幻影，是他弹奏《Satisfaction》和弦的声音。

sentences.en: Arguably the most popular Rolling Stone song ever.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是滚石乐队有史以来最受欢迎的歌曲。

sentences.en: And he said he created that classic guitar riff from his sleep.
sentences.zh: 他说他是从睡梦中创作出了那个经典的吉他即兴重复段。

sentences.en: It was a dream-inspired musical piece of creativity, followed by about 42 minutes of snoring.
sentences.zh: 那是一段梦境激发的音乐创作，随后是大约42分钟的打呼噜声。

sentences.en: Lots of scientific discoveries, though, too, have been birthed by way of dream-sleep-inspired creativity.
sentences.zh: 不过，许多科学发现也是通过梦境和睡眠激发的创造力而诞生的。

sentences.en: Speaking of scientific discoveries, I understand there's a connection between sleep
sentences.zh: 说到科学发现，我听说睡眠与元素周期表的发现之间存在联系。

sentences.en: and the discovery of the periodic table.
sentences.zh: 德米特里·门捷列夫当时正试图理解宇宙中所有已知元素是如何组合在一起的。

sentences.en: Dmitry Mendeleev was trying to understand how all of the known elements in the universe fit together.
And it was his obsession for years.
sentences.zh: 他苦苦思索，却始终找不到答案。

sentences.en: And he struggled, and he couldn't figure it out.
sentences.zh: 他会制作写有不同元素的扑克牌，

sentences.en: He would create playing cards with all of the different elements,
sentences.zh: 并把它们排列起来，看看能否找到某种能将它们组合在一起的方程式。

sentences.en: and he would deal them to see if he could find some equation by way of which they all fit together.
sentences.zh: 显然，故事是这样说的，1869年2月17日，他精疲力竭、沮丧不已，因为无法解开谜题而睡着了。

sentences.en: And apparently, so the story goes, February 17th, 1869, he fell asleep, exhausted, frustrated, couldn't figure it out.
sentences.zh: 就在那里，在他沉睡的大脑中，浮现出了他清醒时的大脑无法预见的解决方案。

sentences.en: And there, in his sleeping brain, emerged the solution that his waking brain could not divine.
sentences.zh: 他开始意识到所有这些旋转的元素成分实际上是如何组合在一起的，

sentences.en: He started to realize how all of these swirling elemental ingredients could actually snap together
sentences.zh: 形成了他所描述的那种神圣的网格，每一行、每一个周期、每一列、每一个族，

sentences.en: in this sort of what he described as a divine grid, where you had each row, each period, and each column, each group,
sentences.zh: 都具有原子和轨道电子特征的逻辑演变。

sentences.en: having this logical progression of atomic and orbiting electron characteristics.
sentences.zh: 他醒来后，写下了这张非凡的表格，

sentences.en: And he woke up, and he penned down this remarkable table,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们现在所说的元素周期表。

sentences.en: the table that we now call the periodic table of elements.
sentences.zh: 他指出，他可能只做了一两处修改。

sentences.en: And he noted that he made just perhaps one or two changes.
sentences.zh: 那份文件至今仍然存在。
你仍然可以看到那件梦境激发的创造力作品。

sentences.en: You can still see that dream-inspired piece of creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我认为这是最值得解决的问题之一。

sentences.en: So, you know, there is one of the greatest, I think, arguable problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 解决它的不是清醒的大脑。

sentences.en: And it wasn't a waking brain that solved it.
sentences.zh: 而是沉睡和做梦的大脑完成了它。

sentences.en: It was a sleeping and a dreaming brain that did it.
Matthew says there are two types of sleep.
Rapid eye movement sleep, also known as REM.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们做梦的时候。
然后是非快速眼动睡眠，或非REM睡眠。

sentences.en: Then there's non-rapid eye movement sleep, or non-REM.
sentences.zh: 这两种睡眠实际上在整晚都在进行着一场争夺大脑主导权的精彩博弈。

sentences.en: And those two types of sleep actually play out in this wonderful battle for brain domination throughout the night.
sentences.zh: 这场大脑战争每90分钟胜负一次，

sentences.en: And that cerebral war is won and lost every 90 minutes,
sentences.zh: 然后每90分钟重复一次，产生我们所说的睡眠周期。

sentences.en: and then replayed every 90 minutes to produce what we call a sleep cycle.
sentences.zh: 你先进入非REM睡眠，然后进入REM睡眠，

sentences.en: And you go down into non-REM sleep first, and then you go up into REM sleep,
and then you repeat the cycle.
sentences.zh: 你说非REM睡眠可能与巩固记忆有关，

sentences.en: You say that non-REM sleep might be implicated or involved in cementing memories,
sentences.zh: 而且有一首流行歌曲可能触及了这个想法。

sentences.en: and that there's a popular song that might get at this idea.
I've come to talk with you again.

sentences.zh: 在我沉睡时留下了种子。

sentences.en: Left its seeds while I was sleeping.
sentences.zh: 而那植入我大脑的幻象，

sentences.en: And the vision that was planted in my brain

sentences.zh: 那么，马修，西蒙和加芬克尔关于非REM睡眠的理解有什么正确之处？

sentences.en: So, Matthew, what do Simon and Garfunkel get right about non-REM sleep?
sentences.zh: 这是最非凡的预言性智慧。

sentences.en: It is prophetic wisdom of the most remarkable kind.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为他们在那里提出的观点领先于时代20到30年。

sentences.en: You know, I think that they were suggesting things there that were 20, 30 years ahead of their time.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，我们在白天会印刻信息。

sentences.en: We now know that we imprint information during the day.
sentences.zh: 我们某种程度上，那颗种子在白天被植入大脑中。

sentences.en: We sort of, that seed is planted there within the brain during the day.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们学习信息。

sentences.en: In other words, we learn information.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，那植入大脑的幻象，

sentences.en: But we also know that that vision that was planted in the brain
sentences.zh: 在寂静之声中，在黑夜的黑暗中，依然留存。

sentences.en: Still remains in the sound of silence, in this, in the dark of night.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，深度的非REM睡眠专门去执行它的记忆功能。

sentences.en: And it's there that specifically deep non-REM sleep goes to perform its memory functions.
sentences.zh: 深度的非REM睡眠几乎按下了那些最近获取的信息片段的保存键。

sentences.en: Deep non-REM sleep almost hits the save button on those recently acquired informational pieces.
sentences.zh: 这样当你第二天早上醒来时，你拥有的是记忆而不是遗忘。

sentences.en: So that when you wake up the next morning, you have remembering rather than forgetting.
sentences.zh: 非REM睡眠的核心在于帮助我们保留信息。

sentences.en: Non-REM is all about helping us retain information.
sentences.zh: 正如我们从滚石乐队的音乐和元素周期表的创造中所看到的，

sentences.en: And as we saw from the music of the Rolling Stones and the creation of the periodic table,
sentences.zh: REM睡眠，即梦境睡眠，激发了创造力。

sentences.en: REM sleep, dream sleep, spurs creativity.
sentences.zh: 但马修说梦还有另一个功能。

sentences.en: But Matthew says dreams also have another function.
sentences.zh: 然而，第二个功能非常不同。

sentences.en: The second function, however, is very different.
sentences.zh: 那个功能似乎是关于情感治疗，或者我所描述的“过夜治疗”。

sentences.en: That function seems to be about emotional therapy or what I would describe as overnight therapy.
sentences.zh: 梦境睡眠提供了一种迷人的神经化学舒缓膏。

sentences.en: Dream sleep provides a fascinating neurochemical soothing balm.
sentences.zh: 正是在梦境睡眠期间，而且只有在梦境睡眠期间，我们的大脑才会关闭一种与压力相关的

sentences.en: It is during dream sleep and only during dream sleep when our brain shuts off a stress-related
sentences.zh: 神经化学物质，叫做去甲肾上腺素。
大家对它在体内的姐妹化学物质都很熟悉。

sentences.en: Now, it's sister chemical everyone will be familiar with in the body.

sentences.zh: 但它在大脑中的版本被称为去甲肾上腺素。

sentences.en: But the version of it upstairs in the brain is called noradrenaline.
sentences.zh: 正是在梦境睡眠期间，这种化学物质实际上被关闭了。

sentences.en: And it's during dream sleep that that chemical is actually shut off.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，在梦境睡眠期间，大脑的情感和记忆中心

sentences.en: But what we also know is that the emotional and memory centers of the brain during dream sleep
sentences.zh: 在活动方面会变得活跃起来。

sentences.en: light up in terms of their activity.
sentences.zh: 因此我们提出，梦境睡眠提供了一个绝佳的机会，我们可以开始

sentences.en: And so we've proposed that dream sleep provides this perfect opportunity where we can start to
sentences.zh: 重新激活和重演痛苦、困难的情感经历。

sentences.en: reactivate and replay painful, difficult emotional experiences.
sentences.zh: 但我们是在一个神经化学上所谓的“安全”环境中进行的。

sentences.en: But we do so in a neurochemically, quote-unquote, safe environment.
sentences.zh: 我们现在了解到，梦境睡眠实际上有助于分离和剥离那些信息体验中痛苦的情感

sentences.en: And we now understand that dream sleep actually helps separate and strip away that painful emotional
sentences.zh: 刺痛感，这样你醒来时对它感觉会好一些。

sentences.en: sting from those informational experiences so that you wake up feeling better about it.
sentences.zh: 你醒来时带着对某个情感事件的记忆，但它本身不再具有情感色彩。

sentences.en: You wake up with a memory of an emotional event but is no longer emotional itself.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种夜间治疗的形式。

sentences.en: It's that form of nocturnal therapy.

sentences.zh: 你好，我是格蕾塔·皮滕格。
格蕾塔是NPR的一名研究员。

sentences.en: Greta is a researcher at NPR.
sentences.zh: 大约八九年前，她与睡眠的关系发生了改变。

sentences.en: And about eight or nine years ago, her relationship with sleep changed.
sentences.zh: 我让她来告诉你这个故事。

sentences.en: I let her tell you the story.
sentences.zh: 我当时在和一个男人约会，他现在是我的丈夫，但当时我们只是在约会。

sentences.en: I had been dating a guy who is now my husband, but at the time we were just dating.

sentences.zh: 那是他唯一的交通工具。

sentences.en: And that was his only form of transportation.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我跟他出去，或者他开车送我去上班什么的，我都会坐在后面，

sentences.en: So whenever I'd go out with him or he'd drive me to work or something, I would ride on the back
sentences.zh: 戴着我自己的头盔之类的东西。

sentences.en: and had my own helmet and stuff.
sentences.zh: 一天深夜，我们从聚会上回家。

sentences.en: Late one night, we were coming home from a party.
And we were in downtown Seattle.
sentences.zh: 街道相当空旷，但我们从红绿灯路口出来时开得很慢。

sentences.en: Well, streets were pretty empty, but we were going pretty slow coming out of a stoplight.
sentences.zh: 一辆大型白色SUV闯了红灯，从左侧撞向了我们。

sentences.en: And a large white SUV ran a red light and crashed into us from the left side.
sentences.zh: 我记得的下一件事就是醒来时仰面躺在一个高出的花坛里，

sentences.en: The next thing I remember is waking up on my back in like an elevated planter,
kind of off on the side of the sidewalk.
You know, there's like the street on one side.
sentences.zh: 另一边有一个小小的挡土墙，上面种着植物和蕨类植物。

sentences.en: And then the other side has like a little kind of retaining wall with like plants and ferns.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一半身体在里面。

sentences.en: And so I was kind of halfway into that.
sentences.zh: 我从摩托车上飞了出去，右大腿撞到了那个混凝土花坛上，

sentences.en: It was about I had flown off the bike and hit my right thigh on that concrete planter
and broke the femur like right in half.
sentences.zh: 当我醒来时，我仰面躺着，双腿垂着，周围有火焰。

sentences.en: And when I woke up, I was on my back with my legs kind of dangling and there was flames around me.
sentences.zh: 然后我想我看到了我当时的男朋友乔伊在人行道上。

sentences.en: And then like that's when I think I saw my then boyfriend, Joey, on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 他似乎也受了伤，但我没有太多时间去想这些事情，

sentences.en: And it was like he was also injured separately, but didn't have much time to think about any of those things
sentences.zh: 因为幸运的是，警察局就在两个街区外。

sentences.en: because luckily the police station was two blocks away.
sentences.zh: 所以警察是第一批赶到的人，他们过来把我们拖了出来。

sentences.en: And so then police were the first people there and came and dragged us out.
sentences.zh: 所以警察是第一批赶到的人，他们过来把我们拖了出来。

sentences.en: The actual crash of the car had punctured the motorcycle.
sentences.zh: 车祸发生时，摩托车被撞出了一个洞。

sentences.en: And then there were the first sound I really remember was an explosion of the motorcycle tank blowing up,
sentences.zh: 我真正记得的第一个声音是摩托车油箱爆炸的巨响，

sentences.en: which was, yeah, I don't trust my memories of how intense it was, but it was very, very scary.
sentences.zh: 那场面……怎么说呢，我不确定自己的记忆是否准确，但当时真的非常、非常可怕。

sentences.en: Joey actually broke the other femur.
sentences.zh: 乔伊其实还断了另一条股骨。

sentences.en: He broke his left femur from the impact of the car.
sentences.zh: 他左侧股骨是因为汽车的撞击而断的。

sentences.en: I broke my right femur from hitting that wall.
sentences.zh: 我右侧股骨是因为撞到了那堵墙。

sentences.en: He also broke a few other bones.
sentences.zh: 他还断了几根别的骨头。

sentences.en: So I stayed in the hospital for maybe four days after surgery.
sentences.zh: 手术后，我在医院住了大概四天。

sentences.en: And he stayed for, I want to say, at least a full week, maybe 10 days because he had a couple surgeries.
sentences.zh: 而他住了……我想至少有一整周，可能十天吧，因为他做了好几次手术。

sentences.en: I didn't sleep pretty much at all, partially because of the painkillers.
sentences.zh: 我几乎完全睡不着，部分原因是止痛药的缘故。

sentences.en: But I think also that's when like bad dreams were starting and I couldn't stop reliving that moment of the crash.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得也是从那时起，噩梦开始出现，我无法停止重温车祸发生的那一刻。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if I had these exact dreams in the hospital, but for a couple years after all of this,
sentences.zh: 我不确定在医院时是否就做了这些具体的梦，但在那之后的好几年里，

sentences.en: I would just keep having dreams about things crashing into me or things running over me.

sentences.en: or whether this is actually the process going awry.
sentences.zh: 还是说这其实是过程出了差错。

sentences.en: And we think it may be the latter because when we look at patients, for example,
sentences.zh: 我们认为可能是后者，因为当我们观察那些患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的患者时，

sentences.zh: 反复出现的噩梦在这些患者身上非常普遍，

sentences.zh: 以至于它们甚至构成了该疾病诊断标准的一部分。

sentences.en: So there is something strange that we've yet to fully understand about particularly emotionally intense trauma dreaMs.

sentences.en: What we think is happening in the case of PTSD is that that chemical that we spoke about
sentences.zh: 我们认为在PTSD病例中发生的情况是，我们之前提到的那种化学物质，

sentences.zh: 即通常在做梦睡眠期间会被关闭的去甲肾上腺素，其水平依然过高。
